records.bodyText:
The South Planning Applications Committee (SPAC) of the Highland Council will consider the Glen Earrach Energy (GEE) application at their meeting next Wednesday (7th Oct).
This may surprise some of you, as we are still in an active consultation period, following the 4th submission of further information by GEE. in September.  
For those you who don't read the Environmental Impact Assessment (Scotland) Regulations 2017, at bedtime - the consultation period for additional or supplementary information for an EIA is a minimum of 30 days. The consultation period remains open until the 5th Oct (next Monday).
Sound planning practice should mean that the Officer would wait until the end of that consultation period and ensure all relevant information is reviewed before completing the report on an application of this nature.
The Highland Council have opted to arbitrarily truncate the statutory minimum consultation period and the Officers report was issued a week prior to consultation deadline.
Clearly the Highland Council don't wish to consider any more responses and/or they are under pressure to get the application to committee.
This has potential ramifications for the outcome of the SPAC meeting, as matters of 'material consideration' may be overlooked!
The decision to unilaterally stop the consultation clock prior to the published deadline could prejudice any decision made next week.
BBC.CO.UK Glen Earrach Pumped Storage Hydro scheme to go before councillors

A six-turbine wind farm near Sanquhar has been approved by Dumfries and Galloway Council.
Rowancraig wind farm, proposed by Koehler Renewable Energy UK (KRE UK), was given the green light by the council’s planning committee on Wednesday, September 30.
The development is planned for Barr Moor, south of Kirkconnel and Kelloholm and around 4km south-west of Sanquhar.
The six turbines will each stand up to 180 metres tall and are expected to generate up to 36MW of electricity.
HERALDSCOTLAND.COM Six-turbine Rowancraig wind farm approved in Dumfries and Galloway

records.bodyText:
PLANS have been submitted for an immense data centre campus in Dumfries and Galloway which, if built, would be the largest in the world. The proposals, submitted to Dumfries and Galloway Council yesterday on behalf of CX Tech Limited, include plans for eight 120MW data centres on land north of the decommissioned nuclear power station at Chapelcross.
However, campaigners have expressed concerns over the plans, particularly as they were submitted just weeks after the Scottish Government agreed to pause decisions on applications for hyperscale data centres until national guidance is produced. They estimate that the centre will require seven million MWh [megawatt-hours] of energy per year, although developers state the centres will be “designed to be operationally net zero”.
“This will put the Scottish Government on the spot – they have said that developers can still put in applications, but also agreed that no decisions will be taken until guidance is in place. They need to immediately make much clearer their position to local authorities and to the developers.
“It is for just these kinds of situations that we need guidance. We can’t have developments landing in Scotland that would use in a year the equivalent of a third of Scotland’s
THENATIONAL.SCOT Plans submitted for 'largest data centre campus in the world' in Scotland

records.title: Scotland Against Spin
records.bodyText:
Rural residents close to a proposed wind farm in Caithness will face “unacceptable” levels of shadow flicker if the development goes ahead . Campaign group Scotland Against Spin says shadow flicker – a visual effect caused when rotating turbines cut through sunlight – should not exceed 30 hours a year.
However, research carried out by a retired engineer who lives near the Olrig Mains Wind Farm site indicates that some properties could experience over 100 hours of the phenomenon and, “in the worst case”, over 180 hours.
Renewable energy company Green Switch Capital announced this month that it was lowering the maximum tip height of the four turbines from 200m to 180m following environmental assessments and feedback from the community.
It insists the Olrig scheme “has been designed to minimise potential effects of shadow flicker through careful turbine placement”.
Scotland Against Spin spokesperson Aileen Jackson, who lives in East Renfrewshire, said: “The standard planning benchmark used across the UK is that shadow flicker from wind turbines at neighbouring dwellings should not exceed 30 minutes per day or 30 hours per year, so this level of flicker is unacceptable.
“While the general rule of thumb suggests shadow flicker is only an issue within 10 rotor diameters of a turbine, evidence proves this is inadequate. Scotland Against Spin has received numerous complaints over the years of flicker well beyond this threshold.
“Personally, I have experienced severe flicker from turbines with a 90m rotor diameter at a distance of 1 km.
“We were advised by environmental health to make videos and keep a diary for a year. This proved that it breached the 30 hours a year guidance and the operator agreed to apply a software fix to shut down the turbines any time flicker occurred, i.e. on clear winter days when the sun was low in the sky.
“But we were very fortunate as often environmental health officers are reluctant to intervene, and operators are unwilling to apply software fixes due to the financial impact of forced downtime.
“We also have problems with flicker at night caused by the blades passing in front of the turbine aviation lights. There is nothing that can be done about this and our environmental health officer told us it was not a statutory nuisance because the frequency was not fast enough to induce an epileptic fit. He advised us to buy blackout curtains!”
https://www.johnogroat-journal.co.uk/.../campaign-group.../

Consequences of the Triumph of the Elitist Climate Agenda of CO2 Reduction:
An Analysis from the Skeptical Perspective
Abstract
From the skeptical climate perspective, the claim that CO2 is a pollutant that must be eliminated at any cost is scientifically weak and politically instrumentalized. CO2 is the gas of life, the basis of photosynthesis and of the planetary greening observed over the last four decades. Imposing sanctions, carbon taxes, consumption limits, and Net Zero targets through coercion would not save the planet but would trigger a cascade of negative consequences of economic, energetic, food-related, social, geopolitical, and cultural nature. This essay develops, in depth, all the bad things that would happen if that agenda were to triumph completely.
Introduction
The official narrative presents decarbonization as inevitable and morally superior. However, climate science is far more uncertain than admitted: climate sensitivity is lower than modeled, models have systematically overestimated warming, and there is no empirical evidence of an ongoing climate crisis attributable to anthropogenic CO2 (Koonin, 2021; Lomborg, 2020). CO2 has risen from 280 ppm to 420 ppm and, far from being a poison, has fertilized the planet, increasing agricultural productivity by more than 15% (Idso, 2022; CO2 Coalition, 2023). The agenda that seeks to sanction its emission starts from a categorical error: confusing an essential trace gas with pollution.
1. ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES: DEINDUSTRIALIZATION AND IMPOVERISHMENT
The first effect of the total triumph of the agenda would be accelerated deindustrialization in the West. The evidence is already visible: more than 40,000 industrial jobs lost in Canada, closure of steel mills in Germany and the UK, and flight of investment to China and India (Energy News Beat, 2024). By artificially making reliable energy more expensive through carbon taxes, emissions trading, and subsidies for intermittent renewables, competitiveness is destroyed. The GDP of the most decarbonized economies shows structural deceleration: the UK went from 2.6% to 1.4% growth and Germany from 2.8% to 0.9% between 1985-1994 and 2015-2024 (BusinessWorld, 2024).
Sanctions and consumption restrictions would generate persistent inflation and stagflation. Energy is a universal input; if it rises, everything rises. The forced transition is top-down Keynesian climate socialism that adds scarcity, inflation, and impoverishment (Lacalle, 2023, cited in Tomorrow's Affairs, 2023). SMEs, unable to absorb regulatory costs and carbon audits, would go bankrupt, concentrating the market in mega-corporations that can afford ESG consultancies. It is green crony capitalism.
The final result is a massive transfer of wealth from the common citizen and the middle class to financial elites who control green funds, carbon credits, and patents for so-called clean technologies.
2. ENERGY CONSEQUENCES: ENERGY POVERTY AND GRID FRAGILITY
Imposing Net Zero means replacing dense, cheap, and dispatchable sources (gas, coal, nuclear) with diffuse and intermittent sources (solar and wind). That does not effectively reduce emissions, but it destroys reliability. Germany and California already experience blackouts and electricity prices 3 to 4 times higher than the U.S. average (Epstein, 2022).
Energy poverty would skyrocket. When electricity goes from $0.08/kWh to $0.35/kWh, poor families must choose between eating or heating. Studies on energy poverty show direct correlation with lower agricultural productivity, school dropout, and health deterioration (Gonzalez-Eguino, 2015; MDPI, 2023). The elitist agenda turns energy, once an abundant good, into a rationed luxury.
Moreover, the grid becomes fragile: overdemand in winter, weather dependence, need for backup with lithium batteries whose mining is highly polluting and controlled by China. Paradoxically, to “save the planet” ecosystems in Africa and Latin America are devastated to extract cobalt, lithium, and nickel.
3. SOCIAL CONSEQUENCES: CONTROL, INEQUALITY, AND LOSS OF FREEDOMS
Reducing consumption by force requires measuring and punishing consumption. Hence the systems of personal carbon footprint, climate passports, coercive 15-minute cities, restrictions on flights, meat, and private cars. What is sold as “sustainability” is, in practice, a digital rationing system managed by unelected elites (World Economic Forum, central banks, Big Tech).
Two classes would be created: a hyper-mobile elite that buys carbon offsets and continues to fly in private jets, and an immobilized mass that must ask permission to travel, eat meat, or turn on heating. The discourse of climate justice produces climate injustice: the poorest in the Global South are condemned to remain without cheap energy, without fertilizers and without mechanization, perpetuating their underdevelopment (CO2 Coalition, 2023).
Collective mental health also suffers. Eco-anxiety induced in children and young people, telling them the world is ending, generates paralysis, guilt, and rejection of having children. It is a profoundly anti-human agenda.
4. FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL CONSEQUENCES: LESS CO2, LESS FOOD
This is the most ignored and most serious consequence. CO2 is aerial fertilizer. Greenhouse enrichment experiments show yield increases of 20-40% in wheat, rice, and tomato at 800 ppm (Idso, 2022). NASA confirms global greening of the planet over the last 35 years precisely because of extra CO2 (Zhu et al., 2016). Reducing CO2 to 280 ppm would condemn agriculture to lose productivity.
Nitrogen reduction policies, as imposed in the Netherlands and Sri Lanka, already caused agricultural collapse and massive protests. Banning nitrogen fertilizers derived from natural gas and sanctioning livestock reduces food supply, makes animal protein more expensive, and pushes hundreds of millions into food insecurity. It is not accidental: less meat consumption is an explicit goal of the agenda.
If the agenda triumphs, eating meat will be a privilege for the rich, the diet will be based on lab ultra-processed foods patented by the same corporations that finance climate alarmism, and food sovereignty will disappear.
5. GEOPOLITICAL CONSEQUENCES: HANDING POWER TO CHINA AND LOSS OF SOVEREIGNTY
The West cannot manufacture solar panels, turbines, batteries, or semiconductors without China. China controls 80% of polysilicon refining, 75% of lithium battery manufacturing, and 60% of wind turbine production (International Energy Agency, 2023). Imposing forced decarbonization is deindustrializing Europe and the U.S. to reindustrialize China. It is geopolitical suicide.
Furthermore, national sovereignty is eroded. Climate targets are imposed via treaties, IMF and World Bank conditionalities, and ESG metrics that dictate from outside what a country can produce. Mexico and Latin America would be pressured not to exploit their own hydrocarbons, remaining as reserves of “environmental services” so Europe can clean its conscience, while buying U.S. gas at a premium price.
6. PARADOXICAL ENVIRONMENTAL CONSEQUENCES: A MORE FRAGILE PLANET
Paradoxically, the “green” agenda is environmentally destructive. A wind farm requires 300 times more materials than an equivalent gas plant (Epstein, 2014). Millions of tons of concrete, steel, non-recyclable fiberglass, and rare earths are needed. Forests in Germany are cut down to install wind turbines. Deserts are covered with panels that alter albedo and kill migratory birds.
Reducing CO2 would not cool the climate in a measurable way — even if the U.S. reached zero emissions tomorrow, the effect on temperature in 2100 would be 0.1°C according to the IPCC’s own models (Lomborg, 2020) — but it would impoverish the planet and make it more vulnerable to extreme cold, which kills 10 times more people than heat.
7. CONCLUSION: THE HUMAN COST OF A FALSE VIRTUE
If the elitist agenda of sanctions and CO2 reduction were to triumph completely, we would not get a cooler planet. We would get a poorer, hungrier, more unequal, more controlled, and more China-dependent planet. We would get blackouts, inflation, industrial unemployment, agricultural collapse, loss of basic freedoms, and a climate priestly caste that decides who can consume and who cannot, while it remains exempt.
Climate skepticism does not deny climate change — climate has always changed — it denies that CO2 is the climate control knob and that impoverishing humanity is the solution. History shows that human prosperity has always depended on cheap, dense, and abundant energy. Replacing it with expensive, diffuse, and rationed energy is a return to pre-modernism, but with carbon-tracking apps.
True progress is not Net Zero. It is more energy for more people, more food thanks to more CO2, more wealth to adapt to any climate, as humanity has always done.
